4.2ND STAGE OF LABOR

Passive:

Full dilatation of cervix in the absence of active pushing

Active:

When baby’s head is visible or involuntary or active pushing with full dilatation of cervix.

Examination:

Vaginal – 1 hourly or according to women’s choice look for:

-Position of head
-Descent
-Caput and molding
•FHR – every 5 min for 1 min after contraction abdominal examination – for frequency, strength and duration of contractions.

Position in 2nd stage:

•She can opt for position whatever she finds comfortable except lying on her back
•Lying on side – choice of spontaneous birth
•Upright position and keeping mobile may be beneficial as it reduces FHR abnormalities, episiotomy rate and improve her birthing.

Pushing in 2nd stage

⇨without epidural
-spontaneous pushing may shorten 2nd stage as compare to directed pushing.
-Directed pushing shorten active 2nd stage in multipara if done while exhaling.
⇨With epidural

Delayed directed pushing by 1 hour after full dilatation reduces risk or forceps or ventouse deliveryDelayed directed pushing by 1 hour after full dilation may shorten active 2nd stage of labor.Nulliparous Multiparous

Directed pushing rather spontaneous

pushing reduces chances of unplanned C/S

Delayed directed pushing up to 2 hours

After full dilatation may shorten active

2nd stage of labor

 

Pushing is ineffective

- Offer support

- Change position

- Empty bladder

- Encourage women.

Interventions to reduce perineal trauma:

•Discuss with women and respect her wishes
•Warm compression in 2nd stage
-Reduce Perineal trauma. offer once presenting part distend the Perineum in 2nd stage
-Apply warm wet compress
•Perineal Massage
-with water soluble lubricant in 2nd stage reduces trauma and need for episiotomy
-Offer if comfortable to women.
•Episiotomy
-Don’t offer routinely
-Don’t reduce risk of trauma
-Done if there is clinical need such as birth with forceps or ventouse or suspected fetal compromise.
-If needed perform Medio lateral episiotomy
-Keep angle 450 – 600 with central axis
-Perform episiotomy with effective, tested analgesia expect in emergency condition because of acute fetal compromise.
•Lidocaine spray:
-Don’t offer to reduce pain
•History of severe perineal trauma
-Inform women that risk in subsequent deliveries is not increased
•History of 3rd or 4th degree tear:
-Make inform choice by taking into account

Current urgency or incontinence symptoms

Degree of previous trauma

Risk of recurrence

Success of repair undertaken

Psychological effect of previous trauma.

History of infibulation

Risk of

1. Difficulty in examination

2. Catheterization

3. Scalp electrode application

4. Delay in 2nd stage

5. Spontaneous lacerations

6. De - infibulation in labour

7. Water birth

Insufficient evidence to support

Delay in 2nd stage of labor:

Delivery is suspected to happen

•Within 3 hours of active 2nd stage in primi
•Within 2 hours of active 2nd stage in Multi

Women with epidural

•Takes up to 2 hours in passive 2nd stage in primigravida
•Takes up to 1 hour in passive 2nd stage in multi

Suspect Delay:

If delivery don’t happen

•After 1 hour of pushing in primigravida
•After 30 minutes of pushing in multigravida

 

Assessment of Mother and baby

-Progress
-Contractions
-Descent of head
-Rotation
-FHR

 

Signs of progress No signs of progress

Present

 

Encourage pushing Amniotomy

 

Still no progress

 

Senior review

(diagnose delay)

Confirm delay:

•After 1 hour of pushing in multi
•After 2 hours of pushing in primi

 

•Escalate senior review
•Transfer of care if needed with full protocols
•Offer support to women

 

 

In person review by obstetrician including

-Fetal well being
-Maternal well being
-Confirmation that there are no signs of obstructed labour
-Confirmation that contractions are infrequent or ineffective

 

 

Start oxytocin after obstetrician’s decision with protocols of oxytocin

 

 

Review every 15 – 30 min.

 

 

Still no delivery or progress within normal duration

-Discuss with women and her partner
-Decide whether to go for ventouse, forceps or C/S
-Decision of intervention on individualized basis

-Decide degree of urgency according to Fetomaternal conditions
-Record time of discussion.
